Project Analyst & Senior Project Analyst, Customer Experience – £50,000-£54,000 – 2 permanent roles
About the Team
Two positions in the Customer Experience & Innovation team, filled at Project Analyst or Senior Project Analyst level depending on experience. The team works with Customer Service, Operations, Technology, Data & Analytics and partners to improve processes, embed new technologies, enhance reporting and drive operational excellence.
Are you?
• Experienced managing or supporting projects, process improvements or change in customer service, technology or operations
• A problem solver who analyses complex information and processes and recommends practical, customer-focused solutions
• Confident communicating with stakeholders and presenting insights and updates
• Highly organised with attention to detail
• Comfortable working independently and across global teams
• Proficient in change management principles and helping colleagues adopt new technology and processes
• Data-driven, with hands-on SQL, Power BI or similar
• Enthusiastic about AI and automation
Key responsibilities
• Analyse customer service processes to automate first-stage customer queries and improve efficiency
• Lead and support CX initiatives from discovery to implementation with measurable outcomes
• Gather, document and translate business requirements into technology solutions using SaaS tools, automation and AI
• Monitor, analyse and report KPIs to evaluate improvements
• Engage stakeholders to drive adoption through change initiatives and training
• Develop governance frameworks, workflows and controls
• Manage project risks, dependencies and timelines
• Support data quality: validation, cleansing and analysis
Benefits: 25 days leave plus 2 floating days; hybrid up to 2 days a week in office; private medical; tuition support.

jd_full:
Investec are looking for a CLM Transformation Analyst (12 month fixed term contract) for a varied transformation role supporting strategic, regulatory and operational change. Immediate focus: a major CLM platform replacement, from a legacy on-premise system to a third-party cloud solution, joining in the implementation phase. Also KYC and financial crime change, Basel 3.1, front-office transformation, process improvement and MI reporting.
What will I be doing?
• Support implementation of the new cloud CLM platform: UAT coordination, defect tracking, vendor management, stakeholder coordination and training ahead of go-live
• Analyse onboarding, client review and offboarding processes for risks, inefficiencies and improvements
• Gather, document and validate business requirements
• Produce current and future-state process maps, procedures, operating models, RACI matrices and BA documentation
• Coordinate workshops, working groups and project activities
• Support regulatory and operational change (KYC, financial crime, Basel 3.1)
• Translate CLM data and reporting requirements for Power BI; support MI, dashboards, KPIs, SLAs and governance reporting
• Monitor progress, risks, controls and deliverables; support post-implementation reviews
Essential
• Strong experience supporting change, transformation or project delivery in a complex operational environment
• Practical experience of testing and UAT, including coordinating activity and tracking defects
• Business analysis experience: requirements, documenting processes
• Excellent organisation and attention to detail
• Confidence engaging stakeholders across business, operations, technology, risk and control
• Process mapping, process improvement and clear documentation
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
• Ability to get up to speed quickly and take ownership
Desirable
• CLM, KYC, AML, onboarding or financial crime knowledge
• Regulatory change or strong risk/control environments
• Coordinating third-party vendors or implementing workflow/automation
• Power BI, Excel, MI and reporting
• KPIs, SLAs and quality measures
• Project delivery methodologies
• Training, communications or change-readiness before go-live
• Benefits tracking, governance forums, post-implementation reviews
Working week: 4 days in the office, 1 remote. 'If this role excites you but you don't meet every requirement, we'd still love to hear from you.'

Position summary
• Reed Smith's Workday implementation is about halfway through and has just begun its second round of end-to-end testing. Join at a pivotal stage and help carry the project through to go-live.

• Bring people together: run focused process walkthroughs with business owners and functional leads to resolve questions and agree future-state processes.

• Enable adoption: give change management and training colleagues validated process information, and review materials for accuracy.
• Land it well: track open issues and decisions, confirm deployment readiness, and prepare a structured handover to business-as-usual.

Requirements (essential)
• Practical HR business analysis skills, particularly as-is/to-be process mapping, stakeholder facilitation, change impact documentation and testing support.
• Experience supporting stakeholders through the later stages of an enterprise system implementation (testing, change readiness, training preparation, deployment).
• Excellent communication skills and confidence running workshops.
• A sharp analytical mind and attention to detail, turning complex information into clear deliverables and visuals.
• A reliable, adaptable and organised approach.
• A relevant degree, or equivalent practical experience in business analysis or systems implementation.

Nice to have
• Experience in professional services.
• Hands-on Workday experience.

jd_full:
URBN – Junior Analyst. London (European Head Office). Commercial finance team.

About Us
URBN UK Limited is part of the URBN Group, a global retailer, with its European Head Office located in London. Its retail offering in Europe takes the form of three brands. With stores in more than 10 European countries and a strong e-commerce presence.

Role Summary
We are looking for a data-driven individual looking to advance their career in a dynamic, fashion-forward retail environment within a commercial finance team, with a view toward business partnering across functional teams.
As our Junior Analyst you will support two key business areas: workforce management for our UK/EU retail business and management accounts for our third-party channels (franchise and wholesale).
The main objective of this role is to champion financial discipline, challenge existing processes, and build BI and AI solutions that improve how we plan and report. Delivering timely, accurate insights to enable effective, profit-focused business decisions is fundamental to this position.

What You'll Be Doing
Workforce Management
• Support the continued development and implementation of the labour scheduling model in UO, AN and FP across the UK and Europe, working with your line manager, Brand Finance and Retail Operations.
• Own the data in the model: maintain and update inputs, check accuracy and integrity, and generate accurate weekly scheduling hours.
• Progress toward leading the model for two brands (AN and FP, with secondary support for UO as required).
• Deliver timely, value-add reporting (weekly, monthly, quarterly) covering store payroll performance (hours and spend) against budget and forecast.
• Support the monthly forecast and the annual budgeting cycle, ensuring labour planning aligns with scheduling model outputs and finance objectives across UO, AN and FP.
• Manage the upload of monthly labour hours into the Live Ledger (our financial reporting system), ensuring data accuracy and integrity.
• Improve existing reporting and move Excel-based reports into Qlik, building and maintaining dashboards yourself, and using AI to automate and enhance store-facing reporting.
• Build strong relationships with brand finance and non-finance contacts, explaining model outputs and challenging assumptions where needed.
• Collaborate with the North America team to share best practice and standardise global process efficiencies.
• Act as the key operational liaison between HRIS/BI teams and Workforce Management.
Financial
• Review and validate monthly actuals and calculate month-end accruals for line manager review.
• Produce clear commentary and performance reports (monthly and quarterly) for wholesale and franchise management accounts, from top-line revenue to operating income.
• Support the monthly forecasting cadence, including financial model maintenance and system data uploads.
• Support the annual budgeting and long-range planning (LRP) processes across full channel P&Ls.
• Identify opportunities to streamline reporting cycles through continuous process improvement and better use of systems.
• Provide ad hoc analytical support and cover routine line manager tasks as required.
• Deliver financial analysis and decision support to cross-functional business partners.

What You'll Need
• Passion for developing a career within a fast-paced retail finance environment
• Demonstrated track record of analysing large data sets or a solid background in accounting and commercial finance
• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and strong PowerPoint skills
• Experience with Qlik, or a proven ability to learn and build in a BI tool such as Qlik or Power BI
• Experience with financial systems such as Hyperion HFM, Essbase or MicroStrategy is desirable
• Proven track record of quickly adopting new software tools and reporting platforms
• Strong ability to translate complex financial concepts into clear insights for non-finance partners
• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
• Strong ability to prioritise effectively and manage stakeholder expectations, with a focus on continuous process improvement

The Perks
• Work-life balance: flexible start and finish times, bring your dog to work.
• Wellbeing: Employee Assistance Program, free gym, private medical insurance.
• Employee discount: up to 40% off at all URBN brands.
• Community: one paid day to volunteer or fundraise for a charity.
• Travel: cycle to work scheme, season ticket loan.
• Continued development: structured support and ongoing learning opportunities.

URBN is an Equal Opportunities Employer committed to diversity and inclusion.

Pay: not stated by the employer (Glassdoor estimate £35k-£62k).

About the role

This role is critical to enabling the successful execution of a complex, multi-year, cross-functional programme.

What you will be doing

• Producing and maintaining core PMO artefacts (including RAIDs, plans, controls, reports, and analysis).
• Providing continuity for agreed programme coordination, reporting and governance activities during periods of Project Manager absence, within delegated authority and established escalation arrangements.
• Demonstrating a pragmatic, can-do attitude, a willingness to dive into the detail when necessary, and a strong sense of teamwork.

Reporting to the project manager on the HR Transformation Programme, this role encompasses:

Governance & Oversight
• Support the programme and its component parts by understanding the sequence of events and their cross-dependencies, enabling impact analysis if milestones move.
• Maintain comprehensive RAID, decision, and change-control logs, with clear owners, target dates, impacts, mitigations, and escalation routes.
• Co-ordinate and facilitate key governance forums, including scheduling, circulation of materials, recording minutes and tracking actions.
• Coordinate programme change requests and support assessment of impacts on scope, schedule, cost, resources, benefits and dependencies.

Planning, Scheduling & Management Support
• Maintain and monitor the integrated programme plan, ensuring alignment with strategic objectives and key milestones.
• Consolidate milestone trackers from individual workstreams into an overall programme view.
• Ensure programme information is accurately captured in the overarching roadmap.
• Coordinate logistics for cross-functional teams, including scheduling and organising meetings and workshops.

Tracking, Reporting & Insights

• Identify, track and manage risks, issues and dependencies, ensuring mitigating plans are in place.

Resource Management

Strategic Data Analyst - Great Ormond Street Hospital Children's Charity
We're looking for a Strategic Data Analyst to join our growing Insight & Performance team. You'll work on projects from forecasting and predictive modelling to supporter lifetime value, audience insight and understanding what drives engagement, helping move beyond reporting what happened to understanding why and what to do next.
We're looking for someone with strong SQL and analytical skills, a curious mind and the ability to turn complex findings into clear recommendations.

Salary
£42,700 per annum; hybrid working with a minimum of 2 days per week in the office. Salaries are not offered above the advertised rate.

Key Responsibilities
• Deliver strategic analysis that helps Fundraising and Marketing teams understand performance, identify opportunities and make informed decisions.
• Develop forecasts, predictive models and segmentation approaches to understand supporter behaviour, lifetime value and opportunities for growth.
• Analyse fundraising campaigns and audience performance, identifying trends, risks and opportunities.
• Work with stakeholders across the charity to turn complex data into clear, actionable recommendations.
• Use insight to support business planning, investment decisions and prioritisation of fundraising activity.
• Evaluate campaigns and experiments.
• Work closely with Selections, Reporting and Data Engineering colleagues to improve audience targeting.
• Explore new analytical techniques and approaches.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise
• Strong SQL skills, with experience analysing and interrogating complex datasets.
• Experience delivering analysis that informs business decisions.
• Experience developing analytical models, forecasts, segmentation or predictive approaches.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Experience working with CRM data and analytical tools to understand customer, supporter or audience behaviour.
• Experience using data visualisation tools such as Power BI.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
• A curious and proactive approach.
• Experience working with fundraising or supporter data.

DBS: a basic DBS check is required.
How to apply: short application form via the apply button. Closing date: 2 December 2026; applications reviewed on an ongoing basis and the role may close early.
Benefits: 30 days' annual leave plus bank holidays, flexible working, enhanced pension, life assurance, health and wellbeing schemes.

Entry-Level | Farnborough | Advisory services

About Us
Egis is a leading global consulting, construction engineering and operating firm. We work together with our clients across every aspect of the built environment, transport and energy to build a more balanced, sustainable, and resilient world. The Egis Group has more than 50 years of experience and a team of 23,500 employees across more than 70 countries.
In the UK, we're proud to be delivering some of the most iconic projects which help connect people, protect our environment, and meet emission reduction targets.
Egis provides comprehensive services to the aviation sector, including advisory, design, engineering, operations, and digital transformation. Operating in more than 100 countries and delivering over 4,000 aviation projects, we partner with airports, air navigation service providers (ANSPs), regulators and governments.

About the Role
We are looking for strategic thinkers who are looking for the opportunity to make a real impact in the aviation industry and build a career as a management consultant supporting Egis' aviation advisory offering. Our clients include airports, ANSPs, governments and regulators, so the project work you do will be varied.

Your responsibilities as a Strategic Analyst would include:
• Providing systematic and structured analysis to our aviation project teams
• Prepare detailed reports, presentations, and visualizations for internal and external stakeholders, summarizing findings and recommendations
• Support the innovation and development of the aviation industry to make it more sustainable, cost-efficient and safe
• Present analysis and recommendations to project teams, clients, and management
• Support our customers in making key business decisions

As our clients are based worldwide, this role will provide you with the opportunity for international travel for face-to-face client interaction.
Sometimes you'll tackle highly analytical assignments; other times, you'll focus on report writing and presentation skills. The consultancy environment can be very fast paced with opportunities emerging at very short notice that will require a flexible, agile approach. We collaborate closely with clients and partners, both at our offices or on client premises.

What do we need from you
Essential
• You are expecting to graduate with a minimum of 2:1 in any of the following subjects: Economics, space, aviation, engineering or another numerate related subject.
• You are good at analysing and presenting data to internal and external stakeholders
• You have excellent report writing skills
• You are a strong communicator
• You are a critical and innovative thinker
• You are equally comfortable collaborating within a team and working autonomously
• You are flexible and adaptable to evolving requirements
• You have strong inter-personal skills
Desirable
• You have a passion for the Aviation industry
• You are able to speak multiple languages

What we can offer you
• Mentorship and career progression opportunities with future global career prospects
• Ongoing learning, access to training and development, including a pathway to professional recognition (e.g., Chartership)
• Competitive salary based on demonstrated skills and experience
• An Employee Assistance Program available to staff, family, and household members

Please upload your cover letter and CV and any other documents that you think will set you apart to our career's portal.
We are an Equal Opportunities employer. Your application will be assessed based purely on your experience, the essential and desirable criteria, and your suitability for the role.

Lloyd's is the world's leading insurance and reinsurance marketplace, bringing together the world's leading risk takers to advance global progress.

Lloyd's are recruiting for an MI Analyst, Member Capital. This is an opportunity to work with the data at the heart of the Lloyd's market. You'll turn complex capital and reserving information into clear, useful insight, helping us understand performance, strengthen our oversight and make better-informed decisions.

What you'll be doing
You'll work across syndicate and member capital, combining data analysis, management information and continuous improvement. You'll:
• Analyse large and complex datasets, identifying trends, outliers and insights that matter
• Help develop and improve management information using tools including Excel, Power Query and Power BI
• Support the processing, validation and audit of capital data submitted through Lloyd's systems
• Build and maintain reporting that tracks capital returns and business forecast submissions
• Develop validation tools and improve how data moves into and out of capital models
• Carry out analysis on member capitalisation and syndicate benchmark capital
• Help answer data and capital-related queries from across the Lloyd's market
• Support the ongoing development of systems used by market participants to assess capital requirements
• Maintain clear documentation, controls and audit information so our processes remain robust
• Collaborate with colleagues across actuarial, risk, catastrophe and syndicate performance teams

What you'll bring
We're interested in what you can do and your potential to develop, not whether you tick every box. You'll ideally bring:
• Strong analytical skills and confidence working with large datasets
• Advanced Excel skills, including experience with Power Query
• Experience with analytical or data tools such as SQL Server, R or Databricks, or a good foundation and the appetite to develop further
• The ability to translate detailed analysis into clear information for different audiences
• Excellent attention to detail and a logical approach to solving problems
• Confidence managing your own priorities and delivering accurate work to deadlines
• The ability to collaborate with people across different disciplines and communicate clearly
• You'll be of graduate calibre, ideally with a mathematical, analytical or finance-based background. Other relevant professional qualifications are welcome.

Being inclusive at Lloyd's
We aim to build a diverse, inclusive environment, open and positive about workplace adjustments, with employee networks, mentoring, volunteering opportunities and investment in professional development.
Support with your application or adjustments is available through Lloyd's adjustments service (this does not register your application).

Job Overview
We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented analyst to join our Audits and Performance Team.
The team plays an important role in helping the establishment understand its performance, recognise good practice, and identify opportunities for improvement. Working with departments across the prison, the team provides insight and assurance that helps maintain high standards across the establishment.
This is an exciting opportunity for someone with strong analytical skills, a keen eye for detail, and a desire to make a positive impact. The role provides exposure to a broad range of operational areas and the opportunity to contribute to meaningful improvements across the establishment.

About the Role
As an Audit and Performance Analyst, you will support the delivery of the establishment's audit and assurance programme, helping to ensure services are delivered safely, effectively, and in line with required standards.
Working closely with teams across the prison, you will contribute to the monitoring of performance, identify opportunities for improvement, and provide assurance that key processes are operating as intended.

Main Duties
• Conduct audits, compliance checks, and audit walkarounds across the establishment in accordance with audit schedules and business requirements
• Support the delivery of assurance activities across a range of operational areas, including Visits, Tool Management, Searching, Intelligence, and External Escorts

• Monitor compliance against contractual, statutory, and operational requirements, and support preparations for internal and external inspections

What we are looking for
• Excellent attention to detail and strong analytical skills
• Clear communication skills and the ability to build effective working relationships
• The ability to work independently, manage priorities, and exercise sound judgement

Deadline for applications is Wednesday 18th November 2026. Following a sift of applications received we will arrange interviews in due course.

Data & Insights Analyst - Mitie, Northampton
Ref: 108701 | Location: Northampton | Employment: Full time

Job Overview
We are looking for a highly capable and commercially minded Contract Data & Insights Analyst to join our Security Operations team.
This is an opportunity to play a key role in developing the contract's data, reporting and analytical capability. Working across Security Operations and the wider contract, you will transform complex operational data into trusted reporting, meaningful insight and effective decision support.
You will work with a broad range of information covering crime, incidents, fraud, colleague safety, operational performance, resourcing, financial performance and service delivery. A central focus will be ensuring the client and operational teams can have confidence in the accuracy, integrity and consistency of the data and reporting used to make decisions.
The role also offers the opportunity to help shape future capabilities, including greater automation, advanced analytics, forecasting and responsible use of AI-enabled solutions.

Main Duties
• Develop and maintain trusted reporting and management information across the contract
• Validate, reconcile and quality assure key datasets, KPIs, dashboards and reporting outputs
• Ensure reporting uses accurate source data, consistent definitions and clearly documented methodologies
• Identify data-quality issues, investigate root causes and work with stakeholders to improve data capture at source
• Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards, reports and visualisations using Power Query and DAX
• Bring together information from multiple systems and data sources to create a consistent view of performance
• Analyse trends, risks, patterns, anomalies and performance issues to support operational and strategic decisions
• Support the development of scalable data models, reporting frameworks and automated validation and reporting processes
• Translate stakeholder requirements into effective analytical solutions and clearly explain the source, definition and limitations of reported information
• Help drive continuous improvement in data governance, reporting, automation and analytical capability

Essential Skills and Experience
• Experience in a data, business intelligence, performance, management information or analytical role
• Experience working with complex datasets from multiple sources and developing effective data models
• Experience of data validation, reconciliation, quality assurance and resolving data discrepancies
• Excellent attention to detail and a demonstrable commitment to data accuracy
• Working knowledge of SQL, relational data concepts, data governance and data lineage
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify meaningful trends and exceptions
• Ability to translate complex analysis into concise, actionable insight for technical and non-technical audiences
• Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, including confidence challenging figures and methodologies where appropriate

Desirable Skills and Experience
• Strong Power BI capability, including Power Query and DAX
• Microsoft Fabric or Microsoft Azure data technologies
• Power Automate, Python, APIs or wider data-integration experience
• ETL, data transformation or data-warehousing knowledge
• Predictive analytics, forecasting, anomaly detection or geospatial analysis
• AI-enabled analytics and automation
• Experience working with crime, security, risk, incident, workforce or operational-performance data

Why This Role Matters
Accuracy and trust in reporting are fundamental to this role. You will help ensure that operational teams, contract leadership and the client can rely on the information used to make important decisions, and help explain why things happened and where action may be required.

Success in the Role
• Accurate, consistent and reliable reporting supported by clear validation controls
• Improved data quality, governance, documentation and traceability
• Meaningful insight that supports operational and strategic decisions
• Reduced manual reporting through controlled and sustainable automation
• Increased client and stakeholder confidence in contract data and reporting

Benefits
• Virtual GP; Salary Finance scheme; flexible benefits platform
• High street discounts, cycle-to-work, life cover up to four times salary
• Enhanced pension, save-as-you-earn, Mitie Matching Share Plan; Mitie Stars awards; training and development

Salary: £28k - £36k (Glassdoor estimate, not employer provided)

Transformation Business Analyst
Permanent

Dacorum Borough Council is currently going through a major Digital Transformation Programme and Housing Transformation Programme. Our aim is to put our customers at the heart of everything we do and to empower our staff by giving them modern tools to deliver consistent and quality council services. To support our journey a new team has been formed to deliver the Transformation Programme - Future Dacorum.

This is an exciting time for Dacorum. If successful, you will be joining an innovative team working closely with services, to make significant changes to the way we deliver to our customers.

This Business Analyst role will form an integral part of the team supporting the overall Digital & Housing Transformation Programmes. You will be supporting services to rethink their processes, identifying opportunities and efficiencies and redesigning processes to reflect these.

A basic check will be undertaken with the Disclosure and Barring Service to ensure that the successful candidate has no relevant convictions.

The deadline for applications will be midnight on the closing date shown in the advert details.
Interviews Date(s): Will be arranged shortly after closing date

Information for applicants on Local Government Reorganisation
The Council is going through a major change as part of Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) and devolution. This means that the district and borough councils in Hertfordshire will be replaced by a smaller number of new unitary councils.
The aim is to make local government simpler and more efficient, improve services for residents, and bring decision-making closer to the communities we serve.

What this means for you
If you join Dacorum Borough Council between now and 31 March 2028, you will move to a new organisation on 1 April 2028. Your role will transfer to the new authority, but the way you work and who you report to may change.
While this may be different from what you are used to, it is also a rare and exciting opportunity to join Dacorum at a time of real change.
You will have the chance to help shape the future of local services and be part of building something new.
The new unitary councils will create opportunities for innovation, growth, and better public services. They will offer a more joined-up and forward-looking working environment for employees.
We are committed to supporting our staff and continuing to deliver high-quality services for residents throughout this change. Together, we are building a better future.

Business Analyst - Liverpool City Council

A bit about us
Liverpool is home to vibrant, diverse and ambitious communities. We are committed to delivering excellent services for residents and are transforming the way we work to create efficient, customer-focused services that meet the needs of our city.
We are looking for an experienced and enthusiastic Business Analyst to join our Customer Experience team and support the delivery of key transformation projects and programmes. This is an exciting opportunity to play a leading role in improving customer journeys, redesigning services and helping shape the future of service delivery across Liverpool City Council.
Working with a wide range of stakeholders, you will provide expert business analysis support, helping services understand current processes, identify opportunities for improvement and design innovative solutions that deliver better outcomes for residents and staff.

In this role, you will:
• Lead the development of customer journey "as-is" maps, gaining a detailed understanding of end-to-end customer and business processes
• Analyse and evaluate data, customer insight and operational information to identify trends, issues and opportunities for improvement
• Work collaboratively with service areas and project teams to design and implement improved "to-be" customer journeys and business processes
• Facilitate workshops, meetings and stakeholder engagement activities to gather requirements and understand business needs
• Produce clear, high-quality process maps, technical specifications, business requirements, reports, presentations and other analytical outputs to inform decision-making
• Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, reduce waste, streamline processes and enhance the customer experience
• Challenge existing ways of working and promote innovative, evidence-based solutions that support service transformation
• Build effective relationships with stakeholders at all levels and work across multidisciplinary teams to deliver agreed outcomes
• Support business change activities, ensuring new processes, systems and ways of working are successfully embedded
• Ensure consistency and quality in customer journey mapping, business analysis practices and continuous improvement methodologies
• Monitor and evaluate the impact of change initiatives and contribute to the delivery of measurable benefits

Please note that this vacancy is fixed term for 18 months to support the delivery of a series of limited term projects.

About you
You will be an experienced Business Analyst with a proven track record of delivering business analysis and service improvement activity within a complex organisation.
You will have:
• Experience of business analysis, process mapping and service redesign
• Strong analytical skills and the ability to interpret data and generate meaningful insight
• Experience of gathering, documenting and managing business requirements
• Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to influence at all levels
• Experience of facilitating workshops and working collaboratively with diverse teams
• The confidence to challenge constructively and create practical, customer-focused solutions
• Excellent report-writing, presentation and problem-solving skills
• A strong commitment to continuous improvement, innovation and positive outcomes for customers and staff

About the programme
This fixed-term role will support Liverpool City Council's Customer Experience Improvement Programme. The successful candidate will lead on business analysis activities, redesigning customer journeys, improving operational processes and helping deliver simpler, more efficient, customer-focused services.

Our offer to you
• At least 31 days holiday plus bank holidays, rising to 35 after 5 years' service
• Agile working (role dependent) - a "Flexibility First" approach
• Local Government Pension Scheme, option to join the AVC Scheme
• Progression, training and learning opportunities
• Health and wellbeing offer including Employee Assistance Programme
• Cycle to Work and Travel Pass schemes, salary sacrifice car lease
• Family friendly policies, discounted gym memberships, volunteering scheme, Medicash

Next steps
Closing date: midnight on Monday 23 November 2026
Shortlisting date: w/c Monday 23 November 2026
Interview date: late November/early December 2026
Interview type: face-to-face
The council may close the vacancy early. Applications are handled through the council's Tribepad system.

Eligibility to work in the UK will be verified in the final stages of the selection process. All candidates must either already have a right to work in the UK before commencing employment or meet the Home Office criteria for Visa sponsorship. Candidates who require sponsorship should evaluate the Home Office eligibility criteria for a Skilled Worker visa before applying.

Salary: £48k - £53k (employer provided)

jd_full:
Job Description

About Aberdeen
Aberdeen Group plc is one of Europe's largest investment companies, and we are built on a long-standing culture of caring about the future and making a positive impact. Together we invest for a better future. We do it to make a difference to the lives of our clients and customers, our employees, society, and our shareholders. Our business is structured around three distinct areas focused on our clients' changing needs: Aberdeen Investments, Aberdeen Adviser, and interactive investor.
As part of Aberdeen Adviser, this role helps deliver the insight, governance and operational excellence that enable advisory businesses to thrive and supports our commitment to Invest in your tomorrow.

About the Department
The PMO team supports the Adviser business by providing governance, portfolio oversight, reporting, resource planning and delivery controls across strategic initiatives. Working closely with delivery, technology and business stakeholders, the team ensures informed decision-making, effective prioritisation and strong execution. The culture is collaborative, accountable and focused on continuous improvement, helping the business deliver better outcomes for advisers and ultimately enabling our clients to be better investors.

About the Role
As the PMO Analyst, you will provide critical support across portfolio governance, reporting, resource management and benefits tracking. You will play an important role in ensuring delivery teams provide accurate, timely and decision-ready information that supports strategic objectives. This is an excellent opportunity to develop your PMO expertise, influence portfolio outcomes and contribute to process improvement initiatives across a dynamic business area. Based in Edinburgh, you will work with a wide range of stakeholders while building valuable experience in portfolio and programme delivery.

Key Responsibilities
• Support governance forums, maintain RAID records, coordinate submissions and ensure compliance with lifecycle and stage-gate controls.
• Maintain portfolio information, including demand, initiatives, milestones, dependencies and roadmap updates.
• Produce portfolio reports, dashboards and management information, providing insight into trends, risks and delivery performance.
• Support resource planning, capacity management and benefits tracking, highlighting constraints, value at risk and planning assumptions.
• Provide practical PMO guidance to project and programme teams while escalating data quality issues, risks and control gaps appropriately.
• Administer PMO tools and contribute to process simplification, automation, standardisation and knowledge sharing.

About the Candidate - Essential Skills
• Experience within a PMO, portfolio, programme or project support environment.
• Good understanding of governance, RAID management, planning, dependencies, resource tracking and benefits management.
• Ability to create clear reports, dashboards, presentations and executive reporting materials.
• Working knowledge of tools such as ServiceNow, Jira, SharePoint, Excel and Power BI, alongside an interest in continuous improvement.

Desirable skills
• Strong analytical skills with the ability to identify trends, exceptions and data quality issues.
• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including the confidence to challenge constructively.

We are proud to be a Disability Confident Committed employer. If you have a disability and would like to apply to one of our UK roles under the Disability Confident Scheme, please notify us by completing the relevant section in our candidate questionnaire.

Our benefits
40 days' annual leave, a 16% employer pension contribution, a discretionary performance-based bonus (where applicable), private healthcare and a range of flexible benefits, including gym discounts, season ticket loans and access to an employee discount portal.

An inclusive way of working
At Aberdeen we've adopted a 'blended working' approach. This approach combines the benefits of face-to-face collaboration, coaching and connecting in our offices with the flexibility of working from home.
If you need assistance with your application, or a reasonable adjustment to your interview arrangements, please let us know and we'll be happy to help.

Salary: not stated (Glassdoor estimate £35k - £50k). Edinburgh, Scotland.

Financial Operations Analyst - Order to Cash & Travel and Expenses - Sage, Newcastle upon Tyne

Job Description
Are you experienced in finance operations and enjoy solving problems, supporting customers and finding better ways to get things done?
We're looking for a Financial Operations Analyst to join our European Finance Shared Services Centre in Newcastle. This is a varied role spanning Order to Cash (O2C) and Travel & Expenses (T&E), giving you the opportunity to build broader finance operations experience while making a real impact on our customers and colleagues.
Your time will typically be split around 60% O2C and 40% T&E, although this may flex as business priorities change. Alongside day-to-day operations, you'll have opportunities to improve processes, support automation and contribute to wider Finance transformation initiatives.

Overview of the team
You'll be part of our European Finance Shared Services Centre, working across our O2C and T&E teams and collaborating with colleagues throughout Finance, Sales, Customer Success and Support.

Summary of your day-to-day
You'll manage O2C activities that help us maximise cash collection and reduce overdue debt, while also supporting employees and managers with expense claims, corporate cards and T&E processes. You'll work with different teams to resolve more complex issues, keep systems and reporting up to date, and make sure processes meet the right controls and compliance requirements. You'll contribute ideas for improving workflows, reporting and automation, including opportunities to use AI and digital tools to reduce manual effort.

Office location
Newcastle upon Tyne. Hybrid working - 3 days per week in our Newcastle office and 2 days from home.

Key Responsibilities
Order to Cash
• Manage customer account activity, helping maximise cash collection and reduce overdue debt
• Investigate and resolve account queries, payment disputes and billing issues
• Support specialist processes including account maintenance, suspensions, cancellations and terminations
• Manage workflow queues, debt management systems, reporting and operational controls
• Partner with Sales, Customer Success, Finance and Support to resolve issues affecting collections
• Act as a point of escalation for specialist O2C processes and help maintain clear process documentation
Travel & Expenses
• Review and validate employee expense claims against company policy and compliance requirements
• Support our corporate credit card programme and respond to employee and manager queries
• Investigate more complex T&E issues and help colleagues navigate expense policies and systems
• Support month-end, reporting, audit and governance activities
• Look for ways to improve the employee experience while reducing manual effort and increasing efficiency
Improvement and transformation
• Identify opportunities to simplify, improve and automate processes across O2C and T&E
• Support dashboards, reporting solutions and workflow improvements
• Get involved in projects, system testing and process change
• Help us adopt AI, automation and other digital solutions across Finance Operations
• Share knowledge and best practice across the wider team

What we're looking for
You don't need to have worked across every aspect of both O2C and T&E. What's important is a solid grounding in finance operations, great customer service and the curiosity to learn and improve how things work.
You'll ideally bring:
• Previous experience within Finance Operations, Shared Services, Order to Cash, Purchase to Pay, Travel & Expenses, or a similar finance environment
• Strong customer service skills and confidence working with a range of stakeholders
• Great attention to detail, with a practical approach to investigating and solving problems
• Good Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel, and the ability to manage competing priorities independently
• Experience working with defined processes, controls and compliance requirements
• Clear written and verbal communication skills and a continuous improvement mindset
• Experience with collections or credit control, Certify, Emburse, Power BI, Power Platform, Sage Intacct, Zuora or other finance and automation platforms would be an advantage, but it isn't essential

Benefits
• Bonuses; up to 8% matched pension contribution plus 2% top-up
• 25 days annual leave with the option to buy up to 5 more, plus 8 bank holidays
• 5 paid volunteering days, 50% income protection, holiday buy and sell
• Health, dental and vision cover; work away scheme for up to 10 weeks a year
• Ongoing training and professional development; hybrid working; Healthy Mind app

About ZILO
ZILO is a financial technology company transforming transfer agency and investor servicing. Our cloud-native platform brings traditional and digital assets together, helping financial institutions modernise their operations.

About the Role
As Product Analyst for Alternative Assets and Private Markets, you will be the analytical and requirements engine behind alternatives within ZILO's Core TA product, turning complex alternatives workflows into clear, testable requirements. You will work with the Product Manager, who owns the roadmap, and the wider product team. You won't need tokenisation experience. We want solid grounding in alternatives or transfer agency operations, a good head for calculation logic and data, and the curiosity to learn how the register and, over time, on-chain structures connect.

This is a hybrid role, with an expectation to attend our Canary Wharf office 2-3 times per week.

What You Will Do
• Define the requirements: business and functional requirements for alternatives capabilities, including user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows and data mappings.
• Break down the Epics into user stories that engineering can build from.
• Specify the calculations: commitments, calls, fees, distribution waterfalls and performance fees, with worked examples.
• Map the processes: current-state and target-state workflows across onboarding, capital calls, distributions, capital accounts, semi-liquid dealing and redemptions, reporting and reconciliation (BPMN or similar).
• Reuse what exists: extend existing Core TA services such as the register, ledger, notifications and API.
• Analyse the data: fund documents, administrator statements, capital account data and valuations to define data models, ingestion rules and validation logic.
• Define eligibility and reporting content: investor eligibility rules, FATCA and CRS reporting data and ILPA formats.
• Support integrations with fund administration systems, the general ledger, distributors and data providers.
• Listen to clients: join workshops and discovery sessions, capture feedback.
• Join the delivery cycle: backlog refinement, sprint planning, tracking delivery against scope.
• Test and accept: design and run UAT, validate outputs and manage defect triage.
• Research and report: track regulatory change and build dashboards covering delivery, data quality, processing efficiency and client outcomes.
• Document clearly: product documentation, process maps and business rules.

Requirements (Essential)
About you
• 3+ years in a product analyst, business analyst or similar role in fintech, wealth technology, asset servicing, transfer agency, fund administration or investment operations
• Working knowledge of alternative assets and private markets, and of investor registers or transfer agency operations
• Curious and self-directed, comfortable where answers are not settled yet
• Collaborative, and you ask good questions

Core analyst skills
• Breaking down a process and writing clear, structured requirements that engineers can build from
• Specifying and testing financial calculations with worked examples
• Writing that works for technical and non-technical readers
• Care for detail where financial accuracy and reconciliation matter
• Working knowledge of agile delivery and the software development lifecycle
• Comfort with Jira and Confluence, or similar tools
• Working in SQL and spreadsheets, and reading API documentation and data schemas. No coding required; basic scripting is a bonus

Alternative assets and private markets

• IRR, MOIC, DPI and TVPI, and ILPA reporting formats
• Estimated and final NAV, and reconciliation to administrator statements

• Explaining the trade-offs to operations, engineering and clients

Transfer agency and semi-liquid

• Dealing windows, gates and redemptions for semi-liquid structures
• Reusing shared platform services instead of building new ones

Shape the Future of Digital: Business Analyst (Temp 12 months) at Kingdom Group

At Kingdom Group, we're evolving to meet the changing needs of our customers and communities. With housing challenges across Scotland, the work we do has never been more important. Our Digital Team is leading an ambitious programme of digital, data, and technology change, helping colleagues across the Kingdom Group make smarter decisions and deliver better services.

To support this vital work, we're recruiting a Business Analyst (Temp 12 Months). This is a brand new role offering the chance to lead complex analysis on multi-workstream digital programmes, shape how change is scoped and delivered, and help us become a more data-informed, digitally enabled organisation, all while supporting our vision of Great Homes, Services, People, and Communities.

This is your opportunity to influence how we work, grow our Business Analysis practice, and join a team committed to delivering as One Kingdom and providing the highest standard of service to all of our customers.

The Role
As a Business Analyst you'll:
• Lead the development of business cases, options appraisals, and benefits frameworks for significant digital investments.
• Own end-to-end requirements analysis for complex, cross-functional programmes, from initial discovery through to solution sign-off.
• Take ownership of requirements definition for major system implementations and upgrades across our digital estate, acting as the primary analytical interface with product and service owners.
• Facilitate senior stakeholder workshops and interviews, applying the right analytical techniques and constructively challenging assumptions to address root causes, not symptoms.
• Translate complex data and findings into clear, compelling narratives, including committee papers and executive briefings.
• Develop and maintain BA standards, templates, and toolkits, mentor colleagues, and raise the profile of business analysis across Kingdom Group.
• You'll work closely with the Digital Manager, senior leaders, and the Data and Analytics colleagues, helping us to scope, deliver, and measure the value of digital change across the organisation.

Why Join Kingdom Group?
At Kingdom Group, every role is about making a difference. Every role directly contributes to improving lives, supporting communities, and delivering positive outcomes for those who rely on us.
Working here means joining a supportive, innovative organisation where your work truly matters. We're proud to hold Investors in People Gold and Investors in Young People Platinum accreditations, reflecting our focus on professional development, employee wellbeing, and creating a workplace where everyone thrives.

What We Offer
A pivotal role at the heart of an ambitious digital transformation, alongside the day-to-day support of an experienced Digital Team. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive, and you'll find a supportive environment that prioritises work-life balance, flexibility, employee wellbeing, and ongoing professional development.

About You
We're looking for someone who:
• Has at least five years' experience as a Business Analyst, with a track record of leading complex analysis on multi-workstream digital programmes.
• Can develop strategic business cases and benefits frameworks, including financial modelling.
• Has led requirements analysis on at least one significant system implementation, end-to-end, with deep expertise in process modelling and documentation using recognised methodologies.
• Manages senior stakeholder relationships with confidence - challenging, influencing, and negotiating constructively.
• Has strong data analysis skills and the ability to translate complex data into clear insight.
• Is an outstanding written and verbal communicator, equally comfortable producing board-level papers and facilitating operational workshops.
• Holds a relevant degree or has equivalent experience.

Ready to Apply?
Apply through our website (kingdomhousing.org.uk/jobs).

Closing Date: Sunday 29 November 2026
Interviews: Will be held on Wednesday 9 December 2026 at our Saltire Office, Pentland Court, Glenrothes, Fife.

Kingdom Group is proud to be an inclusive employer. We welcome applications from everyone and are committed to building a workforce that reflects the communities we serve. Junior Business Design Analyst - Change - Counter Terrorism Policing HQ

Vacancy Reference Number: 23291
Number of Vacancies: 1
(B) OCU: CTPHQ Counter Terrorism Policing Headquarters
Location: West Brompton
Band: Band D
Part/Full Time: Full Time
Hours per Week: 36 hours per week
Type of Contract: Permanent

Job Advert
Salary: The starting salary is £40,519, which includes allowances totalling £3,009. The salary is broken down as £37,510 basic salary, which will increase annually until you reach the top of the scale £40,141. Plus, a location allowance of £2,009 and a non-pensionable allowance of £1,000.
This role does not attract Shift Disturbance Allowance.

Job Description
A Junior Business Design Analyst will leverage new technologies, varied datasets, and specialist operational knowledge to undertake detailed analyses activities to develop evidence-based solutions to some of CTP's most complex challenges. A Junior Business Design Analyst will collaborate and build relationships with a wide variety of stakeholders from across the public sector, playing a pivotal role in reacting and reshaping the country's CT approach.

Key roles and responsibilities include:
• Conduct quantitative and qualitative analysis to define organisational problems, design appropriate solutions, and determine the impact of both on CTP's operating model
• Support the translation of complex organisational problems and solutions into simple compelling narratives
• Lead in the organisation of workshops, stakeholder engagement and other relevant meetings and boards
• Proactively assist in maturing the business design practice, expanding your own and others' skillset, providing assurance, and developing new approaches

A Junior Business Design Analyst will work closely with:
• The Business Design Team, participating in team knowledge sharing and contributing to the development of the Business Design offering within CTPHQ.
• Officers and staff across the CTP Network, to gain an understanding of their operational requirements, challenges and opportunities.
• Programme and Project Teams to ensure that Business Design activity is fully understood and incorporated into the Project Plan and activities.
• Other members of staff within the CTPHQ Change Pillar, particularly in the Project and Programme Management, Business Change and Benefits teams.
• Strategy and Performance colleagues to identify the drivers for organisational change, and to gain appropriate management information to identify and evidence the need for change.
• Finance, HR and Communications business partners within CTPHQ to collate data, identify and manage 'people' impacts as part of design activity.

Essential Skills and Experience:
• An ability to identify, interpret and draw out key insights and recommendations from a variety of quantitative and qualitative data sets
• Highly organised with the ability to manage, prioritise and balance your own workload against deadlines
• Solutions-oriented, innovative, forward-thinking approach to complex business problems
• Able to identify and build confidence with various stakeholders, managing expectations and being able to identify conflicting requirements and priorities

Desirable Skills and Experience:
• An awareness of the value that Operating Model development can provide to an organisation
• An interest in working in an environment that helps shape the Counter Terrorism landscape
• Experience of working with various stakeholders within a large organisation including managing expectations and dealing with conflicting requirements and priorities
• Experience of collecting and analysing data to provide concise and meaningful recommendations
• Experience of working across multiple pieces of work at the same time
• Ability to confidently use Microsoft products (Excel, PowerPoint, Word etc).

The use of AI tools is permitted to support the preparation of your application. However, all submitted materials must accurately reflect your own skills, knowledge and experience.

Vetting
This post requires access to the most sensitive intelligence material on a daily basis. Applicants must hold or be prepared to undergo National Security Vetting (NSV) Security Check (enhanced) (SC(e)) level before taking up the post; with a willingness to undergo Developed Vetting (DV) once in post, if required.

Confidentiality Agreement
Applicants should also be aware of the need to sign a confidentiality agreement on taking up the post.

Flexible working
CTP welcomes applications from candidates seeking flexible working arrangements, such as part-time working, job-share and where the role permits, hybrid working arrangements.

How to apply
The application process requires a comprehensive CV, a Personal Statement, and an online application form. In your Personal Statement, you should explain your interest in the position and illustrate how your skills and experiences make you a suitable candidate. Documents in PDF or Word format, labelled as CV and Personal Statement.
Completed applications must be submitted by 23:55 on 14th December 2026.

Competencies tested at sift: We analyse critically (level 2); We are innovative and open-minded (level 2). Value tested: Accountability.

At Boeing, we innovate and collaborate to make the world a better place. We're committed to fostering an environment for every teammate that's welcoming, respectful and inclusive, with great opportunity for professional growth.

The C-17 International Field Services team based at RAF Brize Norton is seeking a dynamic Program Operations & Business Analyst to drive a wide variety of business and operational outputs.

Position Responsibilities:
In this pivotal role, you will act as the operational "glue" for the Brize Norton site, working closely alongside the on-site leadership team. You will play a central role in delivering key program outputs, executing site-wide plans, and serving as the primary coordinating and communicating point of contact bridging the gap between site leadership, internal teams, and international external stakeholders (including our US-based country management team). This is a fantastic opportunity for a motivated professional looking to expand their commercial acumen and take a significant step forward in their aerospace career.
• Program Rhythm Ownership: Coordinate and lead monthly program operating rhythm meetings, including Business Performance Reviews, Functional Holding-to-Account activities, Change Boards, and Key Performance Indicator (KPI) reviews.
• Financial & Labour Stewardship: Support the Base Manager in executing monthly program financial reviews. You will complete targeted training to step into the Assistant Control Account Manager (ACAM) role, helping oversee a multi-million-pound, labour-focused budget.
• Risk & Opportunity (RIO): Proactively identify program Risks, Issues, and Opportunities (RIO), collaborating with teams to develop robust mitigation or campaign plans.
• Strategic Integration: Assist in developing and integrating programs, plans, strategies, and processes that directly align with current and future business goals.
• Operational Excellence: Drive the site's Continuous Improvement (CI) and Employee Improvement (EI) frameworks, identifying and implementing efficiencies in daily business operations.
• Workforce & Resource Tracking: Manage monthly workforce and headcount reporting requirements to ensure optimal site staffing and labour utilization.
• Procurement & Governance: Oversee site-wide procurement tracking and manage the annual cyber grants process in close coordination with Business Development staff in both the UK and the United States.
• International Stakeholder Management: Partner with the US-based International Program Manager on UK-specific support requirements, supporting monthly Program Management Meetings and driving quarterly performance assessment reports.
• Infrastructure & Continuity: Own the site's Business Continuity Plan, coordinate immediate facility requirements, and assist in developing a long-range facilities strategy.

Basic Qualifications (Required Skills/Experience)
• Previous experience working in a project, programme, or business operations support. A background in Aerospace, Defence, or the MoD sector is highly desirable, but transferable operational experience from other regulated industries is welcome.
• Must hold, or be eligible to obtain, UK Security Clearance (SC) for which the UK Government requires 5 years consecutive UK residency to date and the right to work in the UK.
• High proficiency with MS Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), excellent communication skills, and an eye for detail.
• Self-motivated, highly organized, and comfortable working independently to keep a busy site running smoothly.

Preferred Qualifications (Desired Skills/Experience):
The following areas are highly desirable, but not expected on day one; we are fully prepared to train and upskill the right candidate:
• Prior exposure to Earned Value Management (EVM) principles or workforce/labour utilization tracking.
• Foundational understanding of Risk & Opportunity Management.
• Previous experience supporting formal PMO governance frameworks (such as Change Boards or KPI reviews).

• Excellent Adoption and Parental leave options

• Pension Plan with up to 9% employer contribution
• Short Term Sickness: 100% pay for the first 26 weeks; Long Term Sickness: 66.67% of annual salary from 27th week

About Us
Diamour Jewellers is a Hatton Garden-based jewellery business specialising in diamond engagement rings, wedding bands, bespoke jewellery and fine diamond collections.

The successful candidate will be responsible for analysing business operations, evaluating performance, identifying opportunities for improvement and developing strategies to enhance operational efficiency and support business growth.
Key Responsibilities
• Analyse existing business processes, including jewellery sales, inventory management, procurement, customer service and bespoke order fulfilment.
• Evaluate operational performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, productivity and profitability.
• Conduct market research and analyse customer purchasing trends, competitor activities and developments within the jewellery sector.
• Review online and showroom sales performance and recommend improvements to business processes and customer experience.
• Assess existing stock management, order processing and customer relationship management systems to identify operational improvements.
• Gather and document business requirements for enhancements to internal systems, digital platforms and operational workflows.
• Prepare business cases, feasibility studies and cost-benefit analyses for proposed business improvements and expansion initiatives.
• Develop key performance indicators (KPIs), analyse business data and prepare performance reports for senior management.
• Work closely with management, employees, suppliers and external service providers to identify business requirements and implement agreed improvements.
• Evaluate supplier and procurement processes and recommend improvements to purchasing efficiency and stock availability.
• Monitor the implementation of business improvements, assess outcomes against agreed objectives and recommend further action.
• Provide analytical insights and strategic recommendations to support business planning and long-term commercial development.
Qualifications and Experience
• Bachelor's degree or higher qualification in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Commerce, Economics or a related discipline.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving and organisational skills.
• Ability to analyse business data, evaluate processes and develop practical recommendations.
• Good understanding of business operations, commercial performance and process improvement.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Office and business reporting tools.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to present findings clearly to management.
• Ability to prepare professional reports, business cases and performance assessments.
• Previous experience in business analysis, financial analysis, operations or a commercial environment is desirable.
• Knowledge of retail operations, e-commerce, inventory management or the luxury jewellery sector would be advantageous.
What We Offer
• Competitive annual salary of £35,100.
• Full-time permanent position.
• Opportunity to contribute to the development and growth of the business.
• Supportive and professional working environment.
• Career development opportunities.
• Involvement in business improvement and strategic development projects.

Marketing & Commercial Analyst

For more than 65 years, Ifor Williams Trailers has set the standard for durability, performance and innovation in trailer manufacturing. Paid media

The Digital Inclusion and Skills directorate works on closing the digital divide, routes into digital and tech careers, and talent for AI, cyber and frontier technologies. The DIS Analysis Team (GES, GSR and GSG analysts) owns the Essential Digital Skills Survey, monitoring and evaluation, economic appraisal, evidence synthesis and commissioned research.

TechFirst role

Digital Inclusion Senior Analyst role
• Provide analytical and economic advice to policy colleagues, senior officials and ministers.

Business Analyst
12-month fixed-term contract. £46,000-£50,200 per annum. Birmingham / Hybrid.
GreenSquareAccord is investing in transformation, systems and service delivery, and is looking for an experienced Business Analyst to join the Strategic Delivery and Change team on a 12-month fixed-term contract, working across projects supporting business transformation, new system implementations and operational improvements.
The role
Reporting to the Senior Project and Change Manager, you will combine business-as-usual activity and project work across Finance and the wider organisation: gathering and documenting requirements, mapping current and future processes, facilitating workshops and working with stakeholders. A key part is supporting new finance system projects. You will also support transformation such as Voids, system development and business improvement.
Key responsibilities
• Lead workshops and stakeholder discussions on requirements, processes and improvements.
• Map AS-IS and TO-BE business processes.
• Gather, analyse and document business requirements, including user stories and acceptance criteria.
• Work with Project Managers, the Data Migration Lead and project teams.
• Support new finance system implementations and transformation programmes.
• Identify process gaps and inefficiencies.
• Contribute to testing frameworks so requirements translate into effective testing.
• Maintain process maps, documentation and BA artefacts.
• Build relationships with stakeholders across departments.
About you (ideally)
• Previous experience in a Business Analyst role supporting projects and change.
• Strong AS-IS and TO-BE process mapping.
• Proven experience gathering, documenting and managing requirements.
• Writing user stories and acceptance criteria.
• Confidence facilitating workshops and engaging stakeholders at different levels.
• Supporting systems implementation, transformation or improvement projects.
• Understanding of testing frameworks.
• Strong communication, analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Visio or similar is beneficial; housing, local authority or public-sector experience advantageous but not essential.
What's on offer
• £46,000-£50,200 depending on experience; 12-month fixed-term contract; hybrid with one day a week in the Birmingham office.

Business Insights Analyst - 12 months FTC
Travelers is one of the leading property casualty insurers. Target openings: 2.
The opportunity
The Business Insights Delivery team builds solutions that turn data into insights with well-designed data assets and compelling dashboards and visualisations. • Develop knowledge of business intelligence products and tools.
• Learn to complete root cause analysis and perform solution design.
• Take part in project plans and carry out assigned tasks.

• Support transition to production; document all deliverables.
• Support specification documents for production-ready BI reports and self-service tools.
Ideal candidate
• Basic knowledge of Microsoft suite, SQL, statistical packages or other data tools.
• Written and verbal communication with attention to detail.
• Follows through on tasks; works independently and in a team.
• General knowledge of data analysis / data science concepts.
Must have

jd_full:
Pharmacy Data Analyst
Job summary
Support the operational efficiency of the Pharmacy Department by coordinating fiscal management, performing data analysis and maintaining departmental statistics and reports used by leadership and management.
Duties (original text)
• Publish weekly or monthly dashboards, productivity reports and KPIs; develop and maintain operational reports.
• Ensure departmental billing is accurate and timely; review underpayments or denials with Financial Services; maintain the chargemaster.
• Use benchmarks to show baseline metrics; monitor purchases for contract compliance and pricing; identify savings.
• Monitor monthly budget variance; year-end budget versus spend reconciliation with the general ledger.
• Support Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee with financial data; ensure 340B programme compliance.
• Maintain system databases for formulary changes; analyse ordering, invoices, shipping and inventory; document analytics.
Salary: £33,000 - £42,000 per annum (based on experience). Contract: 2 years.
Revised duties
• Analyse NHS prescription dispensing data, pharmacy service activity and stock utilisation.
• Develop weekly and monthly dashboards, performance reports and KPIs for pharmacy management.
• Analyse NHS reimbursement, service claims and payment records; investigate discrepancies with finance.
• Monitor medicine purchasing, supplier pricing, inventory and stock turnover to cut cost and waste.
• Analyse expenditure and budgets against targets; evaluate Pharmacy First, vaccination and travel health services.
• Maintain pharmacy databases; support compliance with NHS reporting, UK GDPR and information governance.
Qualifications
• Bachelor degree in IT, Business Management, Finance, Accounting or Hospital Administration, or equivalent.
• Strong analytical skills.
• Two years' professional experience in healthcare (preferably pharmacy).
• Direct experience in data analysis and/or healthcare planning preferred.
Job types: Full-time, Permanent. Pay: £15.00-£18.00 per hour. Work location: in person.

Purpose of the role: join the Conflicts team at Addleshaw Goddard to help the firm meet its regulatory obligations by managing and mitigating risk: conflict checks, client inception work, managing client terms and matter specifications, and risk analysis on the firm's publications.

The team sits in the Office of the General Counsel, across Leeds, Manchester, Edinburgh, Glasgow and Dubai.

Responsibilities:
• Review, filter and resolve conflict search results, including legal and commercial analysis of potential conflicts and confidentiality issues; escalate key issues.
• Liaise with PAs, fee earners, partners and the wider conflicts team.
• Manage the team inbox: information barriers, extended reports, ad hoc tasks and compliance queries under supervision.
• Support project work, including workflow development and monitoring of systems and controls.

• Risk and compliance experience in a law firm, accountancy or financial services is preferred but not essential.
• Strong research and critical analysis; sound judgement.
• Ability to work at pace and prioritise.
• Stakeholder relationship building.
• Basic knowledge of the Money Laundering Regulations 2019, Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, UN/UK/US sanctions and the SRA Code of Conduct 2019.
• Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel); Intapp desirable.

Permanent, full time. Locations: Edinburgh, Glasgow, Leeds, Manchester. Salary: competitive.
